obligations.note: release() now returns the earlier release only if it is under one day old (`now - previous.released_at < timedelta(days=1)`). A replay after that falls through and calls _send_disbursement again, because nothing checks the 'released' status, so a second disbursement is sent. The passing sample test test_sampled_release_is_idempotent cannot override this direct violation, and no exception covers it.

Ledger entry ACR-0403 (PAY-2 trace, covers payments.py#release at e5bf6465) has lapsed because release changed behaviour, and it is not relied on. Fresh same-strength (sample) evidence ran on head, but PAY-2 fails on code inspection regardless.
Ticket CHG-25827 is standard and approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-09-28, before review. Its component payments.payments covers the only touched file, payments.py.
The code_review approval is from Sofia Santos, a change_approver for payments. She is a different person from the author, Jonah Weiss.
The approval names head commit d6f3a184, the only commit on the change.

run.json shows success on head d6f3a184: 172 tests, 0 failures or skips, including the registered PAY-2 sample control test. The JUnit timestamp (2026-10-23) and local hostname do not match the CI runner, which is a weak point in the evidence.
payments.py belongs to payments.payments, which is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls/, control tests, ci/) are touched, so no control_owner approval is required.
The change is not an emergency and the ticket type is standard, so no post-implementation review is due.
No exception is claimed or relied on. The register has no entry for PAY-2 or payments.payments, so the PAY-2 deviation is not excused.

summary: The change limits release idempotency to a one-day window. A replayed payment instruction older than 24 hours will therefore send a second disbursement to core banking, which directly violates PAY-2. The passing sample idempotency test does not exercise the expired-window case, and no exception in the register covers this deviation. The process records (ticket, independent approval on head, CI on head) are otherwise in order. The PAY-2 violation alone requires rejection.
